# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Emerson Kimura**
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative
Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of denial of prior authorization — Hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914)**
- **Member name:** Emerson Kimura
- **Member ID:** W623723443
- **Plan:** Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative (Commercial/ACA), Wisconsin
- **Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-03
- **Reference number:** POC-0B7F2515DA-96515

---

## Note on the policy being applied

Before anything else, I want to be clear about one thing: **the denial notice I received does not identify the medical policy or clinical review criteria that were used to deny my surgery.** The notice says only that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. Because the plan has not given me the title of that policy or its actual wording, I am not able to quote the plan's criteria back to it in this letter, and I have not attempted to guess at them. Nothing in this letter should be read as a quotation of the plan's policy. Instead, I am setting out the facts in my medical records and asking the plan to compare them to whatever criteria it actually applied.

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), reference number POC-0B7F2515DA-96515, denied on 2026-08-03 as not meeting the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed to treat my hip.

## What my records show

The decision to deny my surgery was the plan's decision, not my surgeon's and not mine. Medical necessity denials for a procedure like this one generally turn on how long the problem has lasted, what non-surgical treatment has been tried, what the imaging shows, and how much the condition limits daily function. Here is what is in my chart on each of those points:

**How long I have had this problem.** I have had 12 months of progressive pain in the hip. It is not relieved by rest.

**Non-surgical treatment I have completed.** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, together with activity modification, over 8 weeks from 2026-04-30 to 2026-06-25, finishing 16 visits. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-27 that gave me only about 2 weeks of partial relief. In other words, I did not go straight to surgery. I worked through therapy, medication, and an injection first, and the pain came back.

**What the imaging shows.** An MRI arthrogram of the hip on 2026-06-26 showed an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, with an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The same study showed the joint space preserved, Tonnis grade 0. This is a structural finding on imaging, not an unexplained pain complaint.

**What my exam shows.** Provocative testing is positive on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain.

**How this affects my daily life.** I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and with pivoting. I cannot run and I cannot squat.

**Surgical risk factors.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I do not smoke.

I want to underline the combination here, because I believe it is what the plan's own reviewers are looking for: a full year of pain that has not gotten better on its own, a documented and completed course of supervised physical therapy, failed medication and a failed injection, a structural tear and impingement confirmed on MRI arthrogram, a preserved joint with no arthritic change, positive findings on physical exam, and real functional loss. My surgeon has documented that the procedure is needed. If the plan's criteria require documented failure of conservative treatment, documented imaging findings, and documented functional limitation, those items are in the record that was already submitted.

## Request for the criteria the plan applied

**I am requesting, in writing, a copy of the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria that were used to deny this request**, including the policy title and the exact criteria language applied to CPT 29914, and the name and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination. The plan holds those criteria; I do not. I understand that my plan's utilization review is administered by CareSource, with musculoskeletal review performed by TurningPoint, and that the Wisconsin line is (414) 296-6120. I am asking the plan to send me the criteria so that I can address them point by point if this appeal is not approved. Until I receive them, I am responding to a determination whose standard has not been disclosed to me.

## Closing request

I am asking Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative to reconsider and overturn the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) and to approve the procedure as recommended by Dr. Reyes. I am also asking that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with orthopedic surgery expertise.

I understand that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, meaning **by 2027-01-30**, and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that is not the correct destination for member appeals, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed, and I ask that the plan forward this letter to the correct department if it has reached the wrong one.

Please contact me at [my phone number] or [my email address] if anything further is needed. I am glad to have my surgeon's office send additional records on request.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Kimura**
Member ID: W623723443
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [List what you are sending — e.g., copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-03; physical therapy discharge note; MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-06-26; office notes from Dr. Reyes; injection record dated 2026-03-27]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
